items.resumen: Give holiday Google Ads a stronger story, using DAIVID's ranking of 75 Christmas ads where Dogs Trust outscored Amazon. The post A Charity Rescue Dog Outscored Amazon’s Christmas Ad – PPC Accounts Need A Story Before Cyber Week appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.resumen: Snap’s Head of Performance Marketing GTM Rick Lucas and Kitsch CMO Ying Ying Kuang on why relying on last-click attribution hides your best customers, and how Clicks + Deterministic Views (CDV) paint a fuller picture of conversion. Consumer behavior is changing, and marketers hunting for incremental growth need to look beyond traditional discovery. As audiences […] The post Your Next Customer Is in the Chat. items.titulo: Temu owner PDD cuts marketing spend 17% as revenue stalls
items.resumen: Online marketing revenue rose 12% to RMB59.8bn and now tops transaction services, down 12%. Can supply chain spending hold shoppers as promotion budgets shrink?

items.titulo: Google Expands & Clarifies Sexual Content Advertising Policy Examples
items.resumen: Google has again updated its sexual content policy for Google Ads, like it did just last month. This time it added more detailed examples of both prohibited and permitted content across nudity, partial nudity, sexual merchandise, and sexual entertainment.

items.titulo: Bing & Microsoft Ads - Made With AI Label
items.resumen: Microsoft is now showing a new label on some of its ads across Microsoft Advertising and Bing Search named "Made with AI." The label is appended to the image on the ad, at the corner of the image, and says "Made with AI."

items.titulo: Ampersand Is Offloading Its Indie Agency Business To Comcast And Spectrum Following Mass Layoffs
items.resumen: Bridging the gap between linear TV and streaming is apparently easier said than done. Ampersand, a TV ad platform that combines linear and streaming data from national and local markets to unify audience targeting and measurement, is significantly paring back its business, AdExchanger has learned. The company, a joint venture established in 2019 by Comcast, […] The post Ampersand Is Offloading Its Indie Agency Business To Comcast And Spectrum Following Mass Layoffs appeared first on AdExchanger

items.titulo: Alibaba's Taobao and Tmall merchant revenue drops 5% as cloud jumps 53%
items.resumen: Stripped of subsidies now booked against revenue, merchant fees grew 1% as sales and marketing costs fell 38%. Can AI agents for sellers revive Taobao growth?

items.titulo: ChatGPT Card Design
items.resumen: OpenAI may be testing a new card-like design in the ChatGPT interface that previews the different functionality available to users in ChatGPT.

items.titulo: The .seo Top-Level Domain (TLD) May Be Coming Soon
items.resumen: A new top-level domain (TLD) or generic domain extension for .seo may be coming soon. It was applied for by XYZ under ICANN's new gTLD round and then confirmed on the final list following String Confirmation Day in October 2026. It is not yet generally available for standard public registration.

items.resumen: Here is a recap of what happened in the search forums today...

items.titulo: Search News Buzz Video Recap: Google November Core Update Status, FBI Alert On SEO Poisoning, Bing & ChatGPT Web Only Links, Microsoft Ads Bid Upgrade
items.resumen: This week, we covered an update on the Google November 2026 core update. The FBI issued an alert on SEO poisoning and how it infected many with malware. Google Search Console's Search Analytics API added...

items.titulo: Google, ChatGPT & Others AI Engines Provide Coupon Codes
items.resumen: Tis the season for holiday shopping and everyone wants to get a good deal, so you head over to your favorite search or AI engine and ask about coupon codes or promo codes available from that merchant. Google provides them in AI Overviews, ChatGPT provides them in its answers, so do the others - you don't have to go to the coupon websites to get them, you just copy them from the AI response.

items.titulo: Spain's AEPD says marketing chiefs can't double as data protection officers
items.resumen: Spanish law already makes ad firms that profile people appoint a DPO; the 59-page guide flags profit-linked bonuses. When does a budget cut become retaliation?

items.titulo: Q3 In Review: Pay TV Shrinks, Streaming And Sports Step Up
items.resumen: Here's a rundown on the TV and streaming companies (those that remain after all the recent consolidation, that is) that posted their earnings for the three months ending Sept. 30 – and what these reports reveal about the state of TV and media today. The post Q3 In Review: Pay TV Shrinks, Streaming And Sports Step Up appeared first on AdExchanger .

items.titulo: Google says 80% confidence is good enough for directional ad tests
items.resumen: Budget tests now run each arm on half its budget, and a shared budget pilot opened this month. Google's own help pages disagree on how long tests should run.

items.titulo: TikTok’s CSAM Problem; You Can’t Bank On Data Security
items.resumen: Some Spanish advertisers pause TikTok spending due to CSAM concerns; a third-party tech vendor of Chase was the victim of a cyberattack; and Anthropic goes public. The post TikTok’s CSAM Problem; You Can’t Bank On Data Security appeared first on AdExchanger .

items.titulo: Google Search Officially Rolls Out Collapsible Sidebar
items.resumen: Google is now officially rolling out what it calls the "collapsible sidebar" within Google Search. We spotted this a few weeks ago and we called it then the AI Mode sidebar in Google Search. Robby Stein from Google said "New on the Google desktop homepage globally: we're rolling out a collapsible sidebar to easily find & jump back into your recent AI searches."

items.titulo: Model sues RomperJack after 2021 photos became AI-generated Instagram ads
items.resumen: Paid in clothes, with no signed release, Jeffrey Stanfield says RomperJack's new owner made AI video of him. Can a 2021 shoot license a synthetic performance?

items.titulo: Apple lets iOS 27 apps tell websites not to sell or share user data
items.resumen: Off by default, the setting sends Sec-GPC: 1 to every frame and subresource, ad tags included. California counts that signal as an opt-out of sale and sharing.

items.titulo: Apple's Safari preview stops losing analytics beacons when pages close
items.resumen: Analytics and ad tech teams get fixes to iframe timing data and URL-stripping extension rules among 201 changes. Which of them reach shipping Safari, and when?

items.titulo: Ad platforms get their own line in Google Analytics budget plans
items.resumen: Properties need a year of cost data from two channels, Google and non-Google, to qualify. Plans still move no money, and Meridian remains a 360-only alpha.

items.titulo: Databricks lines up nine ad platforms for its customer-value signals
items.resumen: Epsilon, Merkle and Omnicom join Meta, Google and Amazon Ads as partners, yet no release date or price is set. Who controls the data that leaves the lakehouse?

items.titulo: Polaris to pay $150,000 in Minnesota's first data privacy law case
items.resumen: Opt-outs were denied when a verification email went unanswered, and GPC signals missed the page in view. Quarterly tracker audits will now run for three years.

items.titulo: One minute will be enough for Nielsen to credit a radio listener
items.resumen: Radio stations and advertisers in Nielsen PPM markets should see about 20% more measurable ad impressions. Who keeps that gain once the April 2027 data lands?

items.titulo: Cable drops to 31.7% of US TV ad time, lowest in Comscore's series
items.resumen: Broadcast rose 2.3 points to 45.5% and streaming hit a series high of 22.8% as Disney ABC took first by owner. What does that mean for who sells TV ad time?

items.titulo: Mailchimp sells for $3.68bn as Walmart's ad growth slows to 25%
items.resumen: Bending Spoons buys Mailchimp, Walmart and Target post slower ad growth, Microsoft trims ads in its Discover feed and Apple brings privacy signals to apps.

items.titulo: Bending Spoons agrees to buy Mailchimp from Intuit for $3.68bn in cash
items.resumen: Under a third of the roughly $12bn Intuit paid in 2021, with $368m returning as Bending Spoons stock. What does the Vimeo owner's playbook mean for Mailchimp?

items.titulo: Australia bans wagering ads for logged-out users from January 1, 2027
items.resumen: Streamers, social apps and news sites need age checks, logins and an opt-out to keep wagering ads. The ACMA guide shows what it will weigh when it investigates.

items.titulo: IAB Australia survey: 8 of 12 search recruiters expect fewer junior roles
items.resumen: Entry-level roles were as little as 1% of Australian ad vacancies. The paper names three search skills, but who trains juniors if automation does the work?

items.titulo: Ex-Semrush president sets a 10% growth floor for MarTech firms he'd buy
items.resumen: Founders with $3m to $10m in ARR get asked for billing data first; Backlinko's founder brand was valued at zero. What still earns a premium after Adobe-Semrush?

items.titulo: Midterm news fills 12 of 28 debuts on Triton's chart as the top four hold
items.resumen: True Crime reach rose 9.4% to 18.7% and leads among women at Index 145 for podcast buyers. What the genre map tells holiday advertisers, and what it leaves out.

items.titulo: Apple TV takes exclusive US rights to all-female F1 Academy from 2027
items.resumen: US fans will need an Apple TV subscription for every 2027 qualifying session and race. This year the series also streamed free. What happens to those outlets?

items.titulo: Wikipedia and Wikidata join a UN-backed set of six AI building blocks
items.resumen: Local developers, civil society and governments in low-resource settings are the target users. Bots already drive 65% of Wikimedia's heaviest traffic. Who pays?

items.titulo: Character.ai faces 35 states' questions under oath on users' data
items.resumen: Fifteen topics include whether AI models in the $10m Smirks and Pangs deal can reveal users' personal data. Testimony is due November 30, before the auction.

items.titulo: Home Office loses bid to hide that it served Apple a secret notice
items.resumen: Judges found officials authorised briefings to The Times and FT, so most of Apple's 5 grounds can be argued in public. What the notice requires stays sealed.

items.titulo: Voting sites faced 180 times more hack attempts than DDoS, Cloudflare finds
items.resumen: Exploit attempts on US government election sites climbed from 200,000 a day in January to 2 million in October. Why did Election Day itself pass so quietly?

items.titulo: SiriusXM's new hunting and fishing channel leaves out older car radios
items.resumen: Live MLF bass fishing and Gun Stories now air on channel 836 for SiriusXM app and 360L users. Which plans include it, and will it carry outdoor brands' ads?

items.titulo: Recording Academy and SAG-AFTRA back DC cap holding ticket resales to 110%
items.resumen: Brokers list 70-80% of tickets on resale exchanges, where buyer fees average 31%, artist groups say. Judge Nichols has yet to rule ahead of the January 1 start.

items.titulo: Asmongold, a GTA first-timer, rates GTA VI a nine after nine hours
items.resumen: Asmongold's 9-hour GTA VI VOD drew 2,358,707 views and 14,000 comments, topped by an 11,000-like protester claim the video never shows. What are brands buying?

items.titulo: Game: Regulators publish the playbook and almost nobody reads it
items.resumen: Sixteen terms in four groups to close the week. One set comes from a French privacy ruling, and two sets keep trading quantities with each other.

items.titulo: Have a Merry Ads-mas
items.resumen: We use Outlook at AdExchanger, and last Wednesday everything came crashing down. PR people resorted to frantic texts to reach journalists. No emails showed up in my inbox for 18 hours. But ad tech soldiered on. We open the episode with a check in about last week’s historic outage, and some of the surprising takeaways […] The post Have a Merry Ads-mas appeared first on AdExchanger .

items.titulo: Microsoft cuts ads per page 35% in its new Discover feed
items.resumen: Search ads now show beside Bing AI Overviews in every market except China, with no new campaign. Labels on AI-made ads remain the advertiser's legal burden.

items.titulo: Gambling ads reach YouTube Home and Search, 29 days after the Masthead
items.resumen: Fantasy sports operators are held to the US or Canada and prediction markets need certification. What the notice omits about five states Google already bars.

items.titulo: YouTube puts Ask YouTube AI search on TVs and gaming consoles
items.resumen: Phones on the same account now link to the TV without shared Wi-Fi, and a push alert unlocks profiles. What do 12 changes mean for creators and TV advertisers?

items.titulo: Google's $99.99 AI plan now spares up to five more people YouTube ads
items.resumen: Ultra subscribers now share YouTube Premium Family, a $26.99 plan, with their household; AI Pro keeps Lite. What does it mean for YouTube's ad-served reach?

items.titulo: Google shrinks idle tools in Gemini agents to about 26 tokens each
items.resumen: Agent builders on Gemini 3.6 and later can now defer tool schemas, in preview. But each server-side search adds a billed model pass: when do the savings hold?

items.titulo: Gemini can now operate Mac apps in a background window, from $4.99
items.resumen: US English only at launch, on Apple Silicon Macs with macOS Sequoia 15.0 for adults 18+. Google has not said how the agent will look to the sites it visits.

items.titulo: Google charges developers about 10 cents a second for Genie 4 worlds
items.resumen: Developer sessions cap at 120 seconds of 720p video on paid keys only, a day after AI Ultra users got it. Brand IP or real people can end a stream mid-session.

items.titulo: Circana purchase data will shape Trade Desk audiences, then grade them
items.resumen: Two days after Attain, Circana's Sales Lift joins Open Measurement for CPG brands. Due by December 31: can one dataset pick the audience and score the sale?

items.titulo: Ad buyers face longer supply chains under IAB Tech Lab's schain 1.1
items.resumen: DSPs will see hp=0 nodes for firms that only route bid requests, and complete gains a value of 2. What must the sellers.json update due in early 2027 settle?

items.titulo: AWS puts fraud filters and device data inside the ad auction
items.resumen: Pixalate's module maps 770,000+ US streaming shows for DSPs, SSPs and publishers bidding on RTB Fabric. Prices are unpublished, and more vendors are on the way.

items.titulo: Only 18% of auto advertisers say CTV reports show cars sold, Jamloop finds
items.resumen: 73% of 120 auto advertisers target streaming TV with their own sales or registration data, and 77% plan to spend more. Can the reporting keep up with budgets?

items.titulo: Amazon's DVA+ frequency caps count Netflix and Prime Video as one
items.resumen: Netflix PG impressions use up the shared cap yet keep delivering; Fire tablet, Kindle and Twitch SOV ads sit outside it. Do Amazon's savings formulas add up?

items.titulo: One goal per campaign: Amazon's DVA+ primer lists 15 KPIs
items.resumen: Advertisers get 2 awareness, 6 consideration and 7 conversion KPIs to choose from. The same page calls Amazon DSP both DVA+ and Ads Agent. Which name sticks?

items.titulo: Amazon draws 24% of retailer searches but 11% of AI shopping answers
items.resumen: Target turns up in 8% of AI shopping answers on a 5% search share, Walmart in 9% on 12%. Which stores will AI assistants name for Black Friday gift buyers?

items.titulo: Walmart's global ad growth drops to 25% as Flipkart's sale slips a quarter
items.resumen: For brands buying Walmart media, US ads grew 37% with VIZIO and Vibe, and Walmart Connect 36%. With the India sale landing in Q4, can global growth recover?
